_doc: Pattern shapes that cause catastrophic backtracking in a naive glob->regex compiler. Ship 002's finding: a STATIC COMPLEXITY BUDGET CANNOT BOUND THIS (a pattern sitting exactly at the cap still hung >10s, and the budget broke a correct verdict). The only sound fix is a non-backtracking linear-time matcher. Use these to prove one. 2026-08-03: the linear-time matcher closes this whole class — all four probes now resolve in <0.2ms. But two independent checkers then showed that LINEAR IS NOT BOUNDED: cost is O(pattern x value) and BOTH are attacker-controlled, so a big enough paste still froze the tab for 5-13 seconds and a 400MB one crashed it. The scale_probes below are those inputs. They are the lesson the backtracking probes could not teach: a matcher that cannot explode can still be asked to do too much work, and the only sound answers are a measured work budget and refusing oversized input BY NAME. Corpora only grow — never trim either list.

probes.note: ship 002 re-check FAIL — sat at the cap, hung >10s
adjacent **/ runs before the collapse fix

assert: Every probe must resolve (match or no-match) in < ceiling_ms with no UI freeze. A synchronous render() that can exceed this freezes the tab and bypasses try/catch — so the matcher must be linear-time, not merely budgeted. Verify against a wall-clock timer, not a static line count.

scale_probes._doc: Each entry must EITHER resolve within ceiling_ms OR return an explicit refusal naming the limit. A verdict that was never finished, a frozen tab, and a stale previous verdict left on screen are all failures. Measure in a real browser: a synchronous handler blocks the event loop, so wall clock inside the page is the only honest number. Found by the 2026-08-03 checker round against ship 002's rebuild.

probes.shape: one long pattern vs one long value
probes.note: checker A; app's own timing readout
checker B; worst case is when NOTHING matches - include-list logic early-exits on the first match, so a matching corpus hides this
checker B; the UTF-8 encode alone dominated - encode each value ONCE per evaluation, not once per pattern

probes.shape: deep YAML nesting, no glob patterns at all
probes.note: checker B; the PARSER is a second, independent source of freezes - probe it separately from the matcher
reading .value materialises a full JS copy BEFORE any parsing. Check .textLength first - it is O(1) and needs no copy.

scale_probes.assert: Every shape resolves or refuses within ceiling_ms of in-page time, the event loop keeps ticking, and no previous verdict is left on screen while a new input is being evaluated.
